section.quality: Mesh quality, equilibrium and estimated error
fig.error_map: Estimated local error (ZZ indicator): regions where the mesh limits accuracy the most
quality.shape: Element shape (radius ratio ρ = 3·r/R; 1 = regular tetrahedron)
quality.error: Estimated analysis error (ZZ indicator, energy norm)
quality.tet4_note: Linear tetrahedra have constant strain inside the element and are too stiff in bending: with them, displacements and stresses tend to stay below the real ones until the mesh is well refined.
quality.zz_explain: Estimated error (Zienkiewicz–Zhu): energy difference between each element's stress and the stress smoothed at the nodes. It is global; at a point, next to supports and corners, it can be much larger. On the cantilever with an exact solution it underestimated the true error by 1.2 to 1.9×.
quality.histogram_caption: Number of elements per radius-ratio range ρ. Values close to 1 indicate well-proportioned tetrahedra; close to 0, flat or elongated elements.
eq.detail: loads ΣF = {applied}; reactions ΣR = {reactions}; residual |ΣF + ΣR| / |ΣF| = {residual}
eq.detail_supports: Reactions include {load} ({share} of the load) applied on nodes that are also fixed: that part goes straight into the support and CalculiX leaves it out of the reaction totals, so the tool adds it back.
eq.reason.no_load: there are no applied forces to compare
eq.reason.load_types: there are loads the tool does not sum yet (pressure, self-weight, imposed displacement or others)
eq.reason.no_dat: the document has no CalculiX reaction text (ccx_dat_file)
zz.reason.material: the estimate needs a single isotropic material with Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio
zz.reason.elements: the estimate is only computed for tetrahedral meshes (4 or 10 nodes)
warn.equilibrium: The support reactions do not balance the applied loads (residual of {residual} %). Possible causes: the CalculiX reaction text (ccx_dat_file) comes from a run before the current loads, or loads and supports are not as intended. Run the solver again and recreate the report before using the results.
warn.invalid_elements: {n} elements are inverted or degenerate (volume of the wrong sign or zero). The solution has no physical meaning in them: remesh.
progress.quality: Checking mesh, equilibrium and estimated error…
exec.safety_none: not computed: yield strength not given
exec.singular: The maximum stress (point {n}) lies on {label}: it may be a numerical singularity, which grows as the mesh is refined, rather than the real stress in the part.
exec.equilibrium: The reactions do not balance the applied loads (residual of {residual} %): check the model and run the solver again before using the results.
exec.invalid: The mesh has {n} inverted or degenerate elements: remesh before using the results.
assume.short: Linear static analysis, elastic material and ideal supports. Not assessed: fatigue, buckling, contact, plasticity, impact and temperature.
assume.static: Static: loads applied slowly and constant.
assume.small_displacements: Small displacements: equilibrium on the original geometry.
assume.linear_material: {name}: linear elastic, same in every direction (E = {e}, ν = {nu}).
assume.force: Forces spread evenly over the faces.
warn.unsaved: The document had unsaved changes when the report was created: the SHA-256 above is of the file saved on disk, which may differ from what was analysed.

ui.level_desc.quick: Quick summary: the conclusion (meets / does not meet), stress overview, deformed shape, results and criteria. To check in a minute.
ui.level_desc.standard: Standard (daily): the quick summary plus the close-up of the design point, support reactions, points of interest with local error and mesh quality. Only what decides.
ui.level_desc.full: Full (documentation): the standard report plus table of contents, close-ups of every point (supports included), error map, convergence study, mesh histogram and traceability.
fem.error.not_static: This version only reports linear static analyses. The chosen result comes from another analysis type (for example frequency, buckling or thermal) and was not processed.
ma.command_tip: Analyses the part, tries coarse, medium and fine meshes and shows whether this computer can handle the analysis, before creating the FEM mesh.
ma.title: Mesh assistant
ma.no_solid: Pick the part from the list in step 1 (or select it in the view and click “Use the one selected in the view”).
ma.part.thickness_tip: t = 2 × volume ÷ area. For a plate it is the thickness itself. All size suggestions start from it, so they work for parts of any size.
ma.no_issues: No detail much smaller than the part.
ma.issue.thin_wall: Wall of {size} between {where}: {ratio}× thinner than the characteristic thickness ({t}). Probably a modelling leftover: if it is not intended, fix the model before meshing.
ma.issue.small_radius: {count} hole(s) or fillet(s) of radius {size} ({where}): curvature will refine the mesh there.
ma.issue.tiny_edge: {count} edge(s) up to {size} ({where}): they may create very small elements.
ma.issue_tip: Double-click to select in the view.
mesh.reason.thickness: {size}: about {per} element(s) across the characteristic thickness ({t}).
mesh.reason.diagonal: {size}: chunky part, size limited by the diagonal ({d}).
ma.status.skipped: not tried (the previous one does not fit)
ma.status.fixed: (straight edges: there was an inverted element)
ma.test_tip: Generates the 5 meshes in a hidden document (your file does not change) and runs CalculiX on the smaller ones, with a generic support and load, to measure memory and time of this part on this computer. All in separate, watched processes with limits.
ma.create_tip: Creates the part's mesh with the chosen option and generates it (Gmsh). If the assistant already created a mesh for this part, it is updated, not duplicated. Meshes you made are not changed. Ctrl+Z undoes.
ma.tested: Trial finished in {elapsed}. Pick an option (or an objective) and click Create mesh.
ma.failed: Gmsh could not generate the {level} mesh ({reason}). See the technical details.
ma.created_at_root: It is at the document root: drag it into the FEM analysis before solving.
ma.confirm_too_big: The chosen option probably does NOT fit in this computer's memory when solving. Create the mesh anyway?
ma.created_beside: The analysis {analysis} already has the mesh {old}, and FEM accepts only one per analysis: the new one is at the document root. To use it, suppress or delete {old} and drag the new one into the analysis.
ma.objective.memory: The finest mesh that fits in memory
ma.auto_tip: Computes the largest node count that meets the objective (with the model's error margin) and searches the element size that gives that mesh, generating trial meshes.
ma.need_test: Click Try the options first: the objective uses the measurements of this part.
ma.what.create: generating the {level} mesh in your document
ma.auto_done: Automatic mesh for "{objective}": {size}, {nodes} nodes, total solve ~{seconds}. It is selected: click Create mesh.
ma.auto_none: Not even the coarsest mesh meets "{objective}" on this computer. Fix the tiny details of the part, close other programs or pick a larger objective.
mesh.reason.objective: {size}: size computed for the chosen objective.
ma.limit.memory: On this computer the limit is the free memory, not the time: that is why larger time objectives can give the same mesh. Closing other programs frees memory for a finer mesh.
ma.limit.time: Here the limit is the chosen time; there is memory to spare.
warn.line_constraint: {label} acts on edges or vertices (a line or a point). In elasticity theory a support or load on a line or point concentrates the force on a zero area: the stress there is infinite, and the computed value grows every time the mesh is refined, without converging. For reliable stresses near it, apply it to the face the part actually rests on (for example, the cylindrical face of a bolt hole).
ma.issue.line_constraint: {label} acts on edges or vertices ({where}): theoretically the stress there is infinite and does not converge with refinement. For reliable stresses, apply it to the face the part rests on (e.g. the hole's cylindrical face).
ma.refine: Local refinement, where stress concentrates: {curved} hole or fillet face(s) at about 1/5 of the radius (at least half the overall size). Tiny radii (details, see the warnings) and support and load faces get no region: the cost would grow a lot, and the stress at supports is singular and is left out of the report's design stress. Check the local error in the report.
ma.refine_none: No local refinement: no hole or fillet smaller than the mesh. Support and load faces are not refined: the stress there is singular and is left out of the report's design stress.
ma.recommend.before: Recommendation: click Try the options to find out which mesh this computer can handle. By default Medium (about 2 elements across the wall) is selected.
ma.recommend.fine: Fine fits with margin and solves quickly: more accuracy at no risk.
ma.recommend.medium: About 2 elements across the wall: the usual minimum for stresses with quadratic elements. Coarse (1 element) tends to give a high error.
ma.recommend.coarse: Medium does not fit with margin on this computer. Coarse runs, but the error tends to be high: check the estimated error in the report and, if possible, close other programs and test again.
ma.recommend.very_coarse: Only very coarse fits with margin now: good for a first look, not for sizing. Fix the tiny details and close other programs.
fig.marker_colors: Balloons: black = result; orange (round tip) = load; purple (square tip) = support. A load or support on several faces or edges repeats its number, one balloon per visible one.
ma.need_time: This computer's solve time has not been measured yet: click Try the options before using a time objective.
ma.pick_tip: All parts (final solids) of the document. Choosing one analyses it at once.
ma.pick_placeholder: — pick the part from the list —
ma.use_selection: Use the one selected in the view
ma.use_selection_tip: Click the part in the view or in the tree, then here.
ma.predicted_tip: Not meshed in the trial: the numbers come from the law measured on this part, and it clearly does not fit.
ma.src.measured_part: {count} CalculiX trial(s) on this part ({low} to {high} thousand nodes; up to {memory} and {seconds}) · accuracy ±{error} %
ma.src.measured_history: {count} trial(s) on earlier parts ({date}): time is known; this part has not been measured yet
ma.src.measured_none: nothing yet — click Try the options
ma.src.estimated_part: fits with margin up to ~{nodes} nodes on this part
ma.src.estimated_band: fits with margin from ~{low} to ~{high} nodes depending on the part's shape (try to find out)
ma.results_stale: The results already in the document were computed with the previous mesh: solve again before generating the report.
ma.degenerate: Warning: {n} element(s) of this mesh are degenerate (flat or folded); CalculiX will refuse it. Choose another fineness and create the mesh again.
mo.command_tip: Beta version. Solves your analysis, measures the estimated error and refines the mesh only where it is high, repeating until the target or the computer's limit.
mo.title: Optimise mesh by the error (beta)
mo.beta: Beta tool: it works and was validated on examples, but it is still being refined. Check the results and, if anything looks odd, report it on PartReview's GitHub. For everyday use, prefer the Mesh assistant.
mo.intro: Runs YOUR analysis (the FEM workbench's CalculiX, with your supports, loads and material), measures the estimated error of each element and refines the mesh only on the faces where it is high. Repeats until the target error, the chosen time or the memory limit.
mo.need_assistant_mesh: No assistant mesh in an analysis. Create the mesh with the Mesh assistant first (it puts the mesh in the analysis); hand-made meshes are not changed.
mo.singular: Support or load on edges/vertices: the neighbouring faces ({faces}) are not refined, because the theoretical stress there is infinite and the error does not converge. Such systems are ill-conditioned: identical multi-core solves can give slightly different results. Support on faces for reliable results.
mo.corners: Idealised supports (faces fully held) concentrate stress at the edge of the held region, where the error does not converge with refinement (singularity). By Saint-Venant's principle this is local: the target uses the error AWAY from the supports, and the table also shows the global one. Stresses next to the support depend on how it is modelled, not on the mesh.
mo.uses_results: This tool uses calculation results and replaces the document's results on each pass (only after the new solve finished well). Mesh changes can be undone with Ctrl+Z.
mo.goal_note: Memory is checked before each pass with this computer's measurements; a mesh that does not fit is never applied.
mo.start_tip: Each pass: solve, error, refine; the new mesh is tried in a hidden document and applied only if it fits.
mo.reading: Reading the results and computing the error…
mo.stage.trial: pass {n}: trying the refined mesh (hidden document)
mo.stop.memory: Stopped: the next mesh ({nodes} nodes) does not fit with margin in free memory. The best one that fitted is kept.
mo.stop.time: Stopped: the next pass ({nodes} nodes) would exceed the maximum time.
mo.stop.stagnation: Stopped: the error barely fell in the last pass. Usually this is a singularity (support or load on an edge, sharp corner): more refinement does not help; fix the model.
mo.stop.nothing: Stopped: no face needs refinement (the remaining error is in singular regions or inside).
mo.stop.cancelled: Cancelled. The mesh and results of the last complete pass stay in the document.
mo.stop.failed: A process failed (CalculiX or Gmsh). Details:
mo.stop.prerequisite: FreeCAD cannot solve the analysis as it is:
mo.final: Result: estimated error away from supports {error} % with {nodes} nodes, in {elapsed}. Generate the report to see the details.
mo.stop.first_too_big: Not started: the current mesh ({nodes} nodes) needs at least ~{memory} in CalculiX, and that much memory is not free. Create a coarser mesh in the Mesh assistant or close other programs.
mo.stop.killed_memory: CalculiX exceeded the memory limit (it reached {memory}; {free} were free) and was stopped before freezing the computer. The previous results stay in the document. Use a coarser mesh in the Mesh assistant or close other programs.
mo.stop.killed_timeout: CalculiX exceeded the time limit and was stopped. The previous results stay in the document.
fig.boundary: Supports and loads: held regions in purple, loaded regions in orange
ui.show_boundary_tip: Beta. Shows the part in gray with supports painted purple and loads orange, for readers who did not run the analysis. Off by default; not in the Quick summary.
hotspot.stress_regular: Maximum stress away from supports and loads
results.vm_regular: Maximum von Mises stress away from supports and loads
fig.hidden: Points of this quantity hidden from this angle: {items}.
ui.logo_reset_tip: Back to FreeCAD's logo. To make the report without a logo, leave the field empty.
fig.deformed: Deformed shape, color = {field} (displacements magnified {scale}×; gray lines = unloaded part)
points.criteria: Stress: the maximum, the maximum away from supports and up to 2 regions above 60 % of the range. Local error: precision of that value.
assume.regular: “Away from supports and loads” = farther than {distance} from them (rule of thumb).
assume.digits: Values with {n} significant digits, from the estimated error.
results.yield_source.material_uts: from the material: lower than the card's yield
assume.criterion_metal: Von Mises criterion: ductile metals (steel, aluminium, brass).
assume.criterion_polymer: Plastic: von Mises and also Rankine (tension), because PLA, ABS and PETG break with little deformation.
assume.printed: 3D-printed part (PLA, ABS, PETG…) treated as solid and the same in every direction.
assume.uts_used: Limit used: tensile strength, lower than the yield strength in the card.
warn.sharp_corner: Point {n} on a sharp inner corner: possible singularity (Williams, 1952). Model the real corner radius.
exec.sharp_corner: The maximum stress (point {n}) sits on a sharp inner corner: it may be a singularity that grows as the mesh is refined. Model the real corner radius to get a reliable value.
warn.singularity_many: Points {n} on {label}: possible singularity, do not use them for sizing.
warn.sharp_corner_many: Points {n} on sharp inner corners: possible singularity (Williams, 1952). Model the real corner radii.
reactions.intro: Reactions: force of each support on the part (what bolts and fasteners carry, with opposite sign).
reactions.load_on_supports: Part of the load was applied on nodes that are also fixed: the solver does not count it in the reactions above (it goes straight into the support). The equilibrium check in the quality section already includes it.
volume.intro: How much of the part is loaded: share of the volume with von Mises stress above fractions of the material limit. A peak on a few elements and a large loaded region can have the same maximum; this table tells them apart.
conv.intro: Mesh convergence study, recorded by the “Optimise mesh by the error” command: each row is a solved mesh, from the first one to the one used in this report.
conv.converged: Between the last two meshes, the stress away from supports changed {stress} % and the maximum displacement {disp} %: below 5 %, the results are stable with respect to the mesh (usual practical rule in convergence studies).
conv.not_converged: Between the last two meshes, the stress away from supports changed {stress} % and the maximum displacement {disp} %: above 5 %, the results still depend on the mesh. Refine further if the computer allows.
conv.single: Only one mesh was solved: there is no mesh comparison to show convergence.
warn.yield_above_uts: The limit entered ({limit}) is higher than the material card's tensile strength ({uts}): by that card, the material breaks before reaching the limit entered. Check the value; the tension safety factor uses the tensile strength.
volume.none: No part of the volume exceeds {pct} % of the material limit ({limit}): the whole part works with margin.
assume.short_polymer: Plastic (PLA, ABS, PETG…): also checked against the tensile strength (Rankine). A printed part was treated as solid and the same in every direction: between layers the limit is lower.
mo.fc.title: Targets on this computer
mo.fc.before: Shown after the first solve, which measures the current mesh's error and the cost of solving this part.
mo.fc.fits: {target} %: about {nodes} nodes, {memory} of memory, {time} per solve — fits this computer.
mo.fc.too_big: {target} %: about {nodes} nodes, {memory} of memory — does not fit the free memory now ({free}). The optimiser gets as close as fits.
mo.fc.note: Estimate from the theoretical convergence rate (error ∝ N^(−2/3) for quadratic elements); refining only where the error is high usually needs fewer nodes. Singularities can prevent any target.
check.where_regular: away from supports, loads and sharp corners
check.intro: SF = material limit ÷ stress. The smallest design SF governs.
check.none: No conclusion on strength: the material limit was neither given nor found in the material card. Give the yield strength to get the safety factor.
check.meets: MEETS — design safety factor {fs}, equal to or above the required one ({required}). Criterion: {criterion}, {where}.
check.fails: DOES NOT MEET — design safety factor {fs}, below the required one ({required}). Criterion: {criterion}, {where}.
check.exceeds: EXCEEDS THE MATERIAL LIMIT — design safety factor {fs}, below 1 ({criterion}, {where}): the material would yield or break, and above the limit the linear analysis no longer holds.
check.number: Design safety factor: {fs} ({criterion}, {where}). For “meets / does not meet”, give the required safety factor when generating the report.
exec.peak_fs: Point {n}, next to a support, load or sharp corner: {value} (SF {fs}) — depends on the modelling, not in the conclusion.
config.error.required_safety: Invalid required safety factor: use a number of 1 or more (e.g. 2 or 1.5).
ui.required_fs_hint: e.g. 2 — empty = no meets/does not meet
ui.required_fs_tip: Safety factor the design must reach (standard, customer or company rule). With it, the conclusion says “meets” or “does not meet”; without it, only the number is shown.
glossary.design_fs.text: Material limit ÷ design stress: how many times the current load the part would withstand. Below 1: the material yields or breaks.
glossary.design_stress.text: The highest stress away from supports, loads and sharp corners. It settles as the mesh is refined, so it decides the conclusion.
glossary.required_fs.text: Target given by whoever generated the report (standard, customer, company). Only with it does the report say “meets” or “does not meet”.
glossary.singularity.text: Point where the model idealises too much (perfectly rigid support, load on an edge, corner without radius). The stress there grows with every mesh refinement: it is not the real stress.
glossary.von_mises.text: Equivalent stress: sums up the stress state in one number comparable to the yield strength. Usual criterion for metals.
glossary.rankine.text: Compares the largest tension (maximum principal stress) with the tensile strength. Used for plastics, which break without much deformation first.
glossary.error.text: How much the mesh limits the precision: the lower, the better. Next to singularities it is always high, so the report also measures it at each point.
glossary.equilibrium.text: Checks that the support reactions add up to the applied loads. If they do not, the model has an error.
glossary.deformed.text: Displacements enlarged in the figure to be visible (the factor is written below the figure); the real values are on the color scale.
assume.static.better: Repeated or impact loads: assess fatigue or impact separately.
assume.small_displacements.better: Parts that deform a lot (clips, springs, snap fits): turn on geometric nonlinearity in the solver.
assume.linear_material.better: Above the limit the result no longer holds; to study yielding, nonlinear analysis.
assume.criterion_metal.better: Cast iron and brittle materials: Mohr–Coulomb criterion.
assume.criterion_polymer.better: Use the tensile strength of your filament, not the generic one.
assume.no_uts: Plastic without tensile strength in the card: Rankine (tension) not assessed.
assume.no_uts.better: Fill in the tensile strength (UltimateTensileStrength) in the FreeCAD material.
assume.printed.better: The print direction is not in the model. If the load can pull the layers apart, use the filament's interlayer (Z axis) strength as the limit, much lower than in plane.
assume.polymer_time.better: Sustained load (creep) or heat: lower the limit. They lose stiffness near the glass transition: PLA ~60 °C, PETG ~80 °C, ABS ~105 °C.
assume.uts_used.better: Check both values in the material card.
assume.fixed.better: The stress next to them is not real; to assess the fastening, model the bolt or contact.
assume.force.better: Really concentrated load (screw tip, point support): apply it on a face the size of the contact.
assume.mesh.better: Refine and compare, or use “Optimise mesh by the error” (beta).
assume.mesh_error: Results depend on the mesh: estimated error {eta} %.
assume.mesh_error.better: Refine where the error map is high, or use “Optimise mesh by the error” (beta).
assume.not_assessed: Not assessed: fatigue, buckling, contact and preload, plasticity, impact and vibration, temperature, manufacturing defects, nor whether supports, loads and material represent the real case.
exec.error_split: {local} % at the design point ({n}); {eta} % over the whole model, concentrated at supports and loads
warn.density: Density of {name} out of the usual range ({value}): check the unit in the material card. It only affects analyses with self-weight or vibration.
assume.limit_printed: Limit given: {limit}, compared with von Mises.
assume.limit_printed.better: The print direction is not in the model. Without knowing how the layers sit relative to the load, use the filament datasheet's interlayer (Z axis) tensile strength: it is the safe side. Without that value, a conservative rule of thumb: ~1/3 of the in-plane value (e.g. PETG ~45 MPa in plane → ~15 MPa).
warn.stale_mesh: The results were computed with another mesh ({used} nodes); the analysis' current mesh has {now} nodes. Solve again before using this report.
check.margin: By the linear analysis, the load may grow up to {k}× the current one keeping the required SF.
check.reduce: To meet it, lower the design stress by {pct} % (or the load to {k}× the current one), e.g. with more material or larger radii in the region.
assume.limit_metal: Limit given: {limit}, compared with von Mises.
assume.limit_metal.better: Use the guaranteed minimum yield of the standard or the batch certificate, not the typical one. Catalogue references: SAE 1020 hot-rolled steel ~210 MPa, SAE 1045 ~310 MPa, aluminium 6061-T6 ~240 MPa.
assume.limit_user: Limit given: {limit}, compared with von Mises.
assume.limit_user.better: Use the supplier's guaranteed minimum, in the material's weakest direction.
assume.limit_card: Limit from the material card: {limit} (generic value).
assume.limit_card.better: Prefer your supplier's value (metal: batch certificate; filament: datasheet), in the weakest direction.
assume.limit_none: No material limit: no safety factor and no conclusion.
assume.limit_none.better: When generating the report, give the yield strength (metals) or the tensile strength in the weakest direction (printed part: between layers).
assume.fs_required.better: It must cover what this analysis does not see: uncertainty of the load, the material and the manufacturing. Repeated loads call for a fatigue analysis, not only a larger SF.
assume.fs_none: No required SF: the report does not say “meets / does not meet”.
assume.fs_none.better: Use the one of the standard or the customer. Without a standard, design textbooks (e.g. Shigley, Juvinall) recommend larger SFs the more uncertain the load, the material and the model are.
check.reduce_limit: To stay below the limit, lower the design stress by {pct} % (or the load to {k}× the current one), e.g. with more material or larger radii in the region.
assume.short_polymer_no_uts: Plastic (PLA, ABS, PETG…) without tensile strength in the card: Rankine (tension) not assessed. A printed part was treated as solid and the same in every direction: between layers the limit is lower.
assume.printed_given: 3D-printed part (PLA, ABS, PETG…) treated as solid and the same in every direction.
assume.printed_given.better: Infill and number of walls change stiffness and strength: use datasheet values measured with print settings similar to yours.
